answer: Hand out paid jobs by sealed-bid auction, then screen the bids the way road agencies catch rigged paving tenders. A farm that owns many bidders tends to file cover bids: losers bunched just above the winner, winners rotating on a schedule. Bidders showing that tight spread and rotation share one reward weight until reviewed. Evasion: bid truly independently, so the farm undercuts itself and its edge sinks into the ocean of honest bids. Wrongly hit: honest agents on one island of shared pricing code; they get an appeal before the next epoch's horizon, not a ban.
